title: Where the segment filter runs
prompt: The account team wants the orders of business customers, with each customer's name. The data team also wants proof that the segment condition is applied while `customers` is read, not after the join. Write `solve(orders, customers)` to return the orders and the filters pushed into the customers scan.
rules: Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id` (an inner join) and keep rows whose `segment` is `business`. Filtering before or after the join both pass: Catalyst pushes the condition into the customers scan either way.

Return `order_id`, `name`, `total`, plus `customers_filters`: the entries of the `PushedFilters` list on the scan that reads `customers`, as an array of text in alphabetical order (`[B, A]` gives `["A", "B"]`). `with_fact` in the starter adds it.
An order with a missing or unknown customer, or a customer with a missing segment, isn't kept. A customer listed twice gives the order twice.
hints: The physical plan (`executedPlan().toString()`) has one `FileScan` line per table read. The customers scan is the one whose `ReadSchema` includes `segment`.
On that line, the list is the text after `PushedFilters: `, between `[` and the first `]`. Its entries are separated by `, `; sort them.
Catalyst moved the filter below the join, so the segment condition shows up in the customers scan, next to the not-null checks it added.
explanation: Even though the filter is written after the join, Catalyst pushes it below the join to the customers side, and from there into the reader itself. The customers scan's `PushedFilters` is `[IsNotNull(segment), EqualTo(segment,business), IsNotNull(customer_id)]`, which sorted is `EqualTo(segment,business)`, `IsNotNull(customer_id)`, `IsNotNull(segment)`: the segment condition, a not-null check on `segment` (a missing segment can't equal `business`), and a not-null check on the join key (an inner join can't match a missing key). The orders scan only gets `[IsNotNull(customer_id)]`, so taking the first scan in the plan gives the wrong list. To find the right line, look for the scan whose `ReadSchema` has `segment`.
